### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-package`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-package/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class), orderHydrationBatch (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a method of class SchemaRegistry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class), /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-package/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aeedc7f4bff2e540697e0a16fec0bd2a225bb90f` — the merge of head `10c01a418105fedab936a4b17a343fecf621fe04` into base `431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aeedc7f4bff2e540697e0a16fec0bd2a225bb90f && git checkout aeedc7f4bff2e540697e0a16fec0bd2a225bb90f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57 10c01a418105fedab936a4b17a343fecf621fe04 && git checkout -B drift-repro 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57 && git merge --no-ff 10c01a418105fedab936a4b17a343fecf621fe04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 431f065177de0cfc9d682b3b18692132390e0c57` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `10c01a418105fedab936a4b17a343fecf621fe04`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-dependency-missing.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-rehydrate-order.test.ts, packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/core/src/hydration-order.test.ts, packages/core/src/hydration-order.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake-dependencies.test.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-artifact-co-ownership.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/services/service-package/src/hydration-dependency-order.test.ts, packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-package/vitest.config.ts + packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts (`resolvePluginOrder`), packages/cloud-connection/src/local-manifest-source.ts (`InstalledManifestEntry`), packages/objectql/src/index.ts (what objectql re-exports from core), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts at `origin/main` (the `ArtifactObjectNameConflictError` message before the change), .changeset/25792-pre-install-dependency-check.md on `origin/main` (the still-pending D2 changeset), packages/{core,objectql,metadata-core,cloud-connection,services/service-package}/package.json and CHANGELOG.md on `origin/main` (versions and release state), scripts/check-registry-log-declared.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0141-inter-app-dependency-declared-checked-before-install.md (D5, Open items 2, merge questions 3, 4 and 12), the GitHub releases and tags listing. The prose faces (.changeset/25792-dependency-declared-co-ownership.md, content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx, content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx) were read for the claims they make about the code above.

### ① Derived judgments

**CI state at review time (2026-10-26T10:21Z, 47 check-runs on the head).** 25 concluded `success`, 7 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 15 still in progress: Test Core shards 1 to 8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`. Concluded green and load-bearing here: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (runs `check:changeset-no-major` and `check:adr-0087-registration`), `Check Changeset`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Docs`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregator is `success` over skipped shards, as on every PR event. The judgments below are rendered on the diff and what has concluded; the test shards, the workspace typecheck and `Build Core` are the gates still owed, and nothing in the diff was found that predicts them red. This record does not vouch for them.

**A. The co-owner map and its three sources — right.** `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` now computes `coOwnersOf(manifest, selfId, scope)` once, a Map from package id to `CoOwnershipSource`, and both halves of the ADR-0130 D3 pair read it: the namespace gate's `.find(owner is not manifest.id and not coOwners.has(owner))` is byte-unchanged and reads the map's keys, and `refuseCoOwnedObjectNameCollision` takes the map and passes `coOwners.get(ownerId)` into the error. So the relaxation and the refusal cannot disagree about who counts, which is the D3 invariant the card restates. Source by source, against ADR-0141 D5:

- `artifact`: `scope.packageIds` minus `selfId`, exactly the set the old code built. Precedence: an artifact co-owner is set first and never overwritten, so a package that is both co-delivered and declared is reported as `artifact`, which is the stronger proof. Right.
- `dependency`, from P's side: `declaredDependencyIds(manifest)` filtered to ids that are installed (`this.getPackage(id)`) and whose installed `manifest.namespace === N`. A declared but absent parent, or a parent under another namespace, is no co-owner, which is D5's "N is X's namespace" condition and merge question 12's refusal to admit without the parent present. Right.
- `dependency`, from X's side (the reverse arm): every sitting owner of N whose own installed `manifest.dependencies` names `selfId` is a co-owner. A sitting owner is by definition installed and holds N, so no further check is owed. This is D5's "read from either end" (merge question 3), and the upgrade test pins both consequences: a re-registered parent is admitted, and a parent newly defining a name its module owns is refused `DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_OBJECT_NAME` naming the module (`existingPackageId` = the module, `coOwnership: 'dependency'`). Right.
- `sibling`: a sitting owner S of N whose declarations intersect `parents`, where `parents` is P's own declared-installed-holding-N set. So S and P each directly declare one installed Q holding N, which is D5's sibling arm verbatim (merge question 4), direct declarations only, no closure walk. The two negative cases the ADR names are pinned: siblings whose parent is absent, and siblings sharing a utility under another namespace, are both still `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. Right.
- Guards: a shareable namespace, no namespace, or no `selfId` return the artifact set alone. `isShareableNamespace` is the same predicate the namespace gate uses, so the dependency sources cannot admit into `base`/`system`/`sys`. Right.

The relation is one-way in who declares (X declares nothing) and symmetric in who is recognised, as the ADR states. Nothing is persisted; the map is rebuilt from the registry's current rows on every install, so a `PATCH` that deletes a declaration removes the proof at the next related registration, which is D3's stated disposition. The ADR-0130 D1 path is untouched: with no namespace sources the map equals the old set, and `refuseCoOwnedObjectNameCollision`'s `coOwners.size === 0` early return still holds for the single-package case (its comment "No artifact scope, or an artifact carrying one package" is now narrower than the condition it guards, since a declaration can fill the map without a scope; the condition is right, the comment is stale by one clause, not blocking).

**Wording per source — right for all three.** `CO_OWNERSHIP_WORDING` is a closed record over `CoOwnershipSource`. The `artifact` entry reproduces the pre-change message byte for byte ("Object name conflict inside one release artifact: ... — delivered by the same artifact — ... Sharing a namespace across packages in one artifact is allowed (ADR-0130 D1); sharing an object NAME is not (ADR-0130 D3)."), so the existing ADR-0130 D3 tests and any consumer matching that text are unchanged, and the constructor's `coOwnership = 'artifact'` default keeps every pre-existing call site's message. The `dependency` entry says "between packages that share a namespace through a declared dependency ... because one of the two declares the other in `manifest.dependencies` ... (ADR-0141 D5)", which is direction-neutral and therefore correct for both ends of the relation (the refusing test asserts it names "declared dependency" and never "same artifact" or "one release artifact"). The `sibling` entry says "between sibling packages that share a namespace under one declared parent ... because both declare the same installed package". One gap, not blocking: the sibling message does not name the shared parent Q, only the two siblings; the test's `toContain('com.acme.crm')` is satisfied by the sibling ids' prefix and does not pin Q. The card asks for "message worded per co-ownership source", which holds; naming Q would be a kindness for the Console's text. `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` now carries one added sentence naming `manifest.dependencies` as the fix (pinned), the rest of its text unchanged, code and status unchanged. The new `coOwnership` field on `ArtifactObjectNameConflictError` is additive.

**B. `orderHydrationBatch` and the cycle degrade — right, and the degrade is the ruling's own.** The sorter is `resolvePluginOrder` with declared ids as `optionalDependencies`, keyed by node position (`String(index)`), so a second row naming an already-seen id is still a node (`carrierOf` is first-wins for edge targets; the duplicate-row test pins that every row reaches the caller). A declared id resolves to the node carrying it (`packageIds` may hold several, the install-local case), a self-edge is dropped (`carrier !== index`), and an id no node carries is not an edge, which is the `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` reading the ADR says to reuse. Insertion order is preserved where no edge decides (pinned). Strongly connected components are found with an iterative Tarjan; every edge whose two ends lie in one component of size above 1 is removed before `resolvePluginOrder` runs, so the sorter can no longer throw on this input, the cycle's members keep source order among themselves, and their edges to acyclic nodes still hold (pinned: `parent` before `x`, `x` before `y`). `cycles` returns each component's labels in source order for the caller to log.

Is the degrade acceptable under the card's rulings? Yes, it is what they prescribe, not a departure from them. Card item 5: "A cycle degrades to source order with a logged refusal and never throws out of the hydrate." ADR-0141 D5: "The cyclic members degrade to source order for that batch, with the cycle logged as a refusal naming them; the acyclic rest keeps its sorted order, and nothing throws out of the hydrate." Merge question 12: "The sorter's cycle throw is not inherited: cyclic members of a batch fall back to source order with a logged refusal, and the hydrate never throws — the per-entry tolerance both paths have today stands." Both callers log at `error` naming the members and the remedy (remove the closing declaration) and then register every entry: `packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts` (one row = one node, `label` the row's `manifest.id`) and `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin.inDependencyOrder` (one ledger entry = one node, `label` the `manifestId`, `packageIds` from `packages[].manifest` or the manifest itself, which is the same split the D2 check at step 1c' and `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` make). The refinement over the ADR's words (a cycle member still follows its acyclic edges instead of falling to raw source order) is strictly more ordered and never less, so no registration that would have succeeded under raw source order can fail under it. The intra-artifact sort in `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` keeps its throw, as the ADR says it should. ⛔ No second sorter: `hydration-order.ts` sorts only through `resolvePluginOrder`; Tarjan is edge pruning, not ordering. D2 is still not run at either hydrate (the diff touches neither hydrate's registration call, and the cloud-connection D2 suite's "ledger entry whose dependency is absent at boot still re-registers" case is unchanged).

**C. The two #25986 review notes — right.** (i) `found` label: when `rangeAdmitsVersion` returns `null` after the `0.0.0` probe showed some alternative reads, the installed version is now re-read with `readExactVersion`; readable means the range is the undecided side, so `unreadable-range`; unreadable means `unreadable-version`. The test pins the union `lt-5 || latest` (written with the less-than operator) against `7.0.0` as `unreadable-range` with `installedVersion: '7.0.0'`, and `^6.0.0` against `6.1.0-beta.1` as `unreadable-version`. The accept set is unchanged (both are refused as before); only the fact row's side is now right. (ii) The wrapper id: `deliveredIds` is removed from `DeclaredDependencyCheck` and the `delivered` set is built from `delivered[]` ids alone; install-local no longer passes `[manifestId]`. The new test pins a module declaring the wrapper id `com.example.multi` (which names no package) refused `absent`, with nothing written. A wrapper whose id is also one of its packages' ids (`composeStacks(..., { manifest: 'preserve' })`) is unaffected, since that package is in `delivered`. At the head no reader of `deliveredIds` remains anywhere under `packages/` (the three on `origin/main` are all in this diff).

**D. New public surface — right.** `@objectstack/core` gains `orderHydrationBatch`, `declaredDependencyIds` and the types `HydrationNode`, `HydrationOrder` through `export *`; no name collides with an existing core export (none of the four appears elsewhere under `packages/core/src`). `@objectstack/objectql` re-exports only `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` and `ArtifactPackageError` from core, so its published surface gains only `CoOwnershipSource` (a type) and the additive `coOwnership` field. `@objectstack/metadata-core` loses the optional `deliveredIds` input (see ② for why that is legal). Core has no api-surface file to regenerate; `packages/spec` is untouched. The changeset names the two value exports; the types are their inputs and outputs.

**E. The vitest env line — right and machine-required.** `scripts/check-registry-log-declared.mjs` demands `env: { OS_REGISTRY_LOG: LEVEL }` in the package-root vitest config of every package whose suite builds a `SchemaRegistry`; `hydration-dependency-order.test.ts` now does. `warn` is the level the other harnesses use. `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is green on the head.

**F. Claims outside these inputs.** The HotCRM precondition paragraph (every `crm` companion declares `app.objectstack.hotcrm` at `d91c7b0`) is outside this brief's inputs; what the code pins is that if it holds, the sibling arm admits each companion beside the app and beside each other, and the intra-artifact declaration is judged for presence only by D2.

### ② Semver level

**Levels.** The changeset introduces `patch` on `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-package`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which are exactly the five published (`private: false`, all at 18.1.0) packages the diff moves; docs and the changeset publish nothing. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone, and `none` takes `patch`. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (`check:changeset-no-major`, `check:adr-0087-registration`) are green on the head.

**`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right, and it is the line the PR body and the changeset both carry.** The widening: install acceptance (a module declaring its app, or a sibling under one declared parent, used to be refused `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` and now installs), plus the new `@objectstack/core` exports. The narrowing: install-local refuses a module that declares only its artifact wrapper's id, and `DeclaredDependencyCheck.deliveredIds` is removed. Per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are true and both are read". It is.

**The narrowing is of an unreleased surface — confirmed from the in-repo release state, so it is legal under the arm with no migration owed.** `deliveredIds`, `checkDeclaredDependencies` and `DEPENDENCY_MISSING` all landed with #25986 (merge `3446d43d40`, 2026-10-26T08:58Z). Every moved package is at 18.1.0 on `origin/main`; the latest GitHub release is `@objectstack/*@18.1.0`, published 2026-10-24T09:13Z from `e649c2d91e`, two days before that merge; no tag contains `3446d43d40`; the 18.1.0 entries of `packages/metadata-core/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/cloud-connection/CHANGELOG.md` contain no `DEPENDENCY_MISSING`, `deliveredIds` or `rangeAdmitsVersion`; and `.changeset/25792-pre-install-dependency-check.md` (the D2 changeset) is still pending in `.changeset/` on `origin/main`, which is the state `changeset version` leaves until the next release consumes it. So no published tarball exposes `deliveredIds`, and no consumer can have called it. AGENTS.md item 3's "removing anything an author can write ... puts the FROM → TO mapping ... in the body" has no FROM to map, and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker is the right disposition. The dev's choice to still carry the `(narrowing)` arm and the `**BREAKING**` banner is the conservative reading (the two changesets will publish in one release, and the D5 entry explicitly says the D2 check is "not-yet-released"), and `check-adr-0087-registration` accepts it with the one marker it carries. One consequence to know, not blocking: the CHANGELOG a reader greps at the next release will carry both entries under one version, the D2 entry describing presence-only delivery and the D5 entry correcting the wrapper-id arm; the D5 entry's own sentence makes that readable.

**`Metadata-protocol: none` stands.** `ManifestSchema.dependencies` keeps `z.record(z.string(), z.string())`; nothing an author writes changes shape, accepted value or meaning. What changes is what the install act and the boot do with the declaration already defined (co-ownership and order). No `packages/spec` edit. The `(narrowing)` arm beside `none` and `patch` is the combination `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` admits (a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition).

**Carriers.** The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, both declaration lines and a "What changes for you" section; the PR body's `Declarations` section repeats both lines with the same values.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`open_questions`: none in the report.** Confirmed: the only decision the D2 report carried (items 6a/6b) is now #26000 (`domain:spec`, `pm:queue`, an issue not a PR), and this diff makes no spec change that would pre-empt it: `declaredDependencyIds` reads the record spelling only and returns `[]` for the array shape (pinned), so neither `PackageDependencySchema` nor `AppManifestSchema.dependencies` gains a reader here. D8 item 2 (`optional` never read) holds by construction.

**Dev flags and out-of-scope findings.**

- *Dogfood `authz-probe-blind-spot`, the `i18n.ts` row.* Same row as on #25986; the dev states both files are unchanged from `origin/main 3518664cb6`, and this diff touches neither `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts` nor the census test (17 files, none of them). The head's dogfood shard check-runs are `skipped` on a PR event, as before. Carrier stays as filed.
- *First reading 2 (rehydrate order across paths).* Read from the code, not instrumented: each hydrate now sorts its own batch; the `kernel:ready` seals and the ledger rehydrate run on the same hook in registration order with no declared edge between the install-local plugin and `ObjectQLPlugin`; the residual case (two `sys_packages` siblings whose parent is only in the install-local ledger) is the one ADR-0141 Open items 2 names as the card's residual reading, and the reverse arm means the later-hydrated parent is still admitted beside the first sibling. Reported, not solved; the ADR places it as a reading, not a build item. Accepted as filed.
- *First reading 6 (the standalone module's artifact `type`).* Not measured here; the dev routes it to the HotCRM lane with reading 7. Accepted as filed; nothing in this diff depends on it (`coOwnersOf` and both sorters read `namespace` and `dependencies`, never `type`).
- *First readings 3 and 4.* Reading 3 (a declared id naming no installable package) was answered on #25986 by the HotCRM measurement (the only declared id is `app.objectstack.hotcrm`); reading 4 (`enabled: false` on X) has not been reported by either PR, and D2 by design does not judge enablement (ADR-0141 D2, Open items 4). It remains a reading on the card, not a build item; escalated to the seat as an open reading, not a condition on this PR.
- *`Fixes #25792` vs `Part of`.* The body says `Part of` because items 3 and 6 are not closed by this PR; `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green. Right as written; see the item ledger below.
- *Deviations from the claim.* None found: no `ui/**` edit (17 files, none under `ui/`), no `packages/spec/**` edit, every touched path inside the claim's file surface (`packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts` callers includes the new `hydration-order.ts`), the declaration line matches the measurement the seat already ruled on #25986.

**Card #25792 item ledger, with this slice plus #25986 (merged `3446d43d40`).**

| Card item | Closed by | Remaining |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1. D2 pre-install check at the three install acts, `422 DEPENDENCY_MISSING` | #25986 (merged); #26054 corrects two D2 facts (the `found` side, the wrapper id) | none |
| 2. The range reader (`rangeAdmitsVersion`, shared parsing, stated grammar) | #25986 (merged) | none |
| 3. The Console refusal text (「请先安装 HotCRM 6.x」) | neither PR; triage 6398501495 routed it to objectui's own card if the copy needs a new string, and the claim scoped it out (⛔ no `ui/**`) | open on this card as an outside-repo item unless the seat reads the triage routing as closing it here; no objectui card number is in these inputs |
